details:
Updated 28 October 2026

After visiting certain sequences of worlds in PCVR, VRChat enters a persistent degraded state. Worlds that normally run smoothly become dramatically slower, and restarting VRChat restores performance. Moving to a lighter world can make the problem less noticeable, but returning to an affected world exposes it again.

I have reproduced this on two identical laptops using both Steam Link and Virtual Desktop. **SteamVR was running in both cases**, so changing streaming clients did not isolate SteamVR from the problem. Lowering SteamVR resolution and shadow settings has not materially improved the severe state.

I have not reproduced the same severe collapse in desktop mode. New desktop captures also lack the rendering-thread signature found in the degraded PCVR captures, although the loading histories were not controlled enough to establish that desktop mode is completely unaffected.

To reproduce, visit these worlds in order during one PCVR session without restarting VRChat:

1. [Displace](https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_59e75193-4507-4064-8dd7-ad7fa9de717f) — launch here as the home world.

2. [OT&T Penthouse](https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_3fc26f42-ce27-47cb-9ec0-a03330306809).

3. [The first of the month](https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_c9ceb2f9-1bd2-4a74-96a9-5bb9d3f34d18).

4. [Abandoned Mall](https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_1d65dbb4-cd63-4ccb-86b6-04368a88d087).

5. In Abandoned Mall, respawn until you appear in the Food Court. Rotate so the entrance is on your right, then enable the **VRChat personal mirror**. I observe approximately 15 FPS.

This shortened sequence has reproduced the collapse every time I have tried it. I did not record an exact trial count or fixed dwell times.

Optionally, turn the personal mirror off and continue to [Pokemon Pocket TCG](https://vrchat.com/home/world/wrld_3faab157-32cd-4706-b2b9-d92e4ba8130d). The persistent slowdown is particularly apparent there without a mirror.

Expected behavior is comparable performance when returning to the same scene, viewpoint and settings. Instead, affected scenes remain severely slower until I restart VRChat.

My saved before/after traces were collected in Pokemon Pocket TCG following an earlier, longer world-hopping sequence. The shorter route above was identified afterward; it was not the route used for those captures.

Earlier checks in Pokemon Pocket TCG showed approximately 105–116 FPS in a fresh client versus approximately **15 FPS in the degraded state**, alone with mirrors off. For the matched October 26 captures, I used the same avatar, viewpoint, settings and power conditions, with Steam Link and VRChat focused. The captures came from separate VRChat process lifetimes. BAD was approximately 15 FPS; GOOD was performing normally, but its exact FPS was not recorded.

Analysis of seven retained seconds from each capture shows:

| Measurement | GOOD | BAD |

|---|---:|---:|

| Render-thread samples containing the identified D3D11 Map stack | 27 / 4,247 | 4,469 / 5,188 |

| Share of render-thread CPU samples | 0.64% | 86.14% |

| Samples at the identified NVIDIA polling instruction | 31 | 4,049 |

| Average GPU power | 169 W | 63 W |

| Average GPU graphics clock | 2.34 GHz | 2.74 GHz |

The degraded rendering thread spends much of its sampled CPU execution in a graphics-driver polling path beneath D3D11 Map. This pattern is present throughout the BAD interval, including its first second.

These are **CPU sampling measurements, not Map-call counts or individual call durations**. They locate an active bottleneck but do not establish which resource or condition is involved, what initiates the degraded state, or which component is responsible.

Additional queue analysis links increased submission activity to a VRChat-owned D3D11 queue: 9,155 versus 217,223 event-450 records in the matched windows. These counts use a VRChat event-header PID filter and are not draw counts, GPU completions, or exhaustive queue totals.

The October 28 desktop comparison provides a useful contrast. A loaded desktop capture after world-hopping and a later capture after restarting VRChat showed approximately 226 and 233 application presents per second, respectively. Map-linked render-thread sample shares were approximately 0.65% and 0.71%, far below the severe PCVR result. Application presents are not headset-delivered FPS, and the differing session histories limit this comparison.

For engineering reference, the sampled path is `UnityPlayer → D3D11 Map → nvwgf2umx`. Analysis of the matching UnityPlayer binary places the call site in a dynamic, CPU-write constant-buffer update path using `WRITE_DISCARD`, followed by a copy and Unmap. Relevant offsets in the captured binaries include:

- D3D11 Map stack: `d3d11.dll+0x165651`.

- UnityPlayer caller return RVAs: `+0x8e5150`, `+0x8e525c`, and `+0x8ec17c`.

- NVIDIA hot sampled instruction: `nvwgf2umx.dll+0x59886e`, within a polling loop containing `PAUSE` at `+0x59886c`.

The captured environment was:

- Lenovo Legion Pro 7 16AFR10H; Ryzen 9 9955HX3D; RTX 5080 Laptop GPU with 16 GB VRAM; 32 GB RAM.

- VRChat `2026.4.1-1935-a61ceb9d89-Release`, Steam open-beta branch.

- Unity `6000.0.67f1-DWR`, Direct3D 11.

- NVIDIA `610.62` / Windows driver `32.0.16.1062`.

- Windows 11 Pro build `10.0.26300`; SteamVR `2.18.4`.

Please investigate the persistent state created by the reproduction sequence and the identified Unity rendering path. An internal capture of Map entry/return times, call frequency, resource descriptors and relevant synchronization dependencies could distinguish slower calls from increased call volume and identify what prevents progress. A supported profiling method for the protected client would also help.

I have saved GOOD/BAD ETLs, sampled stacks, GPU telemetry, filtered VRChat/SteamVR log events, and queue/resource analyses locally. Privacy-reviewed extracts can be prepared for an agreed support channel; the raw captures have not been uploaded.
title: [1935]Severe, persistent PCVR performance collapse after changing worlds or avatars — reproducible route
